title: Not Happy
text: I regret purchasing the annual subscription for $99.99. The app frequently crashes while scanning receipts, though it does save your progress upon restarting. It lacks essential features like organizing receipts by month or day and does not provide totals or visual spending graphs. Additionally, there are no export options to common formats like PDF or Excel, not even email making it hard to manage finances effectively. Given its limitations, the price feels excessive; a more reasonable annual fee would be around $30. I can't recommend this app in its current state. Skip do not download until features are added.

title: Too many bugs and lacks features
text:
• can’t delete receipts or reports
• the date after you scan a receipt is always one day prior to the date on the receipt so you have to manually change it 
• can’t search expenses by the month, date, category, or total amount only by the name
• the reports have the wrong dates (this time, one day after the saved date)
• the data is accessible even after you sign out
• you can save future dates in expenses (like if you have a receipt from the future)

The concept is great and has potential, but it needs to be better quality. Currently it looks like an app some kid made for a school project. There are much better apps out there for managing finances.

I have tried all the receipt apps, and really like the interface and scan quality of this one, but I have to go through hundreds of receipts and fixing the merchant name and date on each one is not much better than manually scanning everything. title: Requires too much manual manipulation
text: I currently have credit and debit as my budget tracking app. This app exports expenses easily to credit and debit, but when I scan receipts I would say it only recognizes the correct date, total, merchant about 50 to 60% of the time. Some of the receipts it never gets correct no matter how many different ways I try to scan it. Consequently I have to manually edit many of the purchases which makes this app less efficient for me. Increasing the accuracy or helping the app to learn receipts from stores I frequent (CVS receipt seemed to confuse it) would make it a time saver. The other feature that would be helpful is to get the app to recognize which account (credit card and which one, cash, etc) was charged and include that in the information about the purchase. Currently this app seems only marginally more effective than manual entry to me so I did not purchase the subscription.

title: Ok for very basic basics
text: This app is alright for tracking expenses and capturing receipts and invoices and then running a report for tax purposes. You can categorize expenses by type per their limited list and can add notes for each receipt. You can scan receipts they the app or upload thru the camera photo function. The bad aspect of this app is once the expenses are added and reports built (By the way, you can only create 2 reports in the free version) there is no way to sort by category, amount , date, vendor, etc. it’s essentially a list of chronological receipts based on the date they were added. This makes it extremely difficult for verification of recurring expenses that may occur weekly or monthly to ensure you’ve captured everything. It’s basically a list you must mull thru and no way to search or sort.  Not the best, but works for very basic capture and storing and A report. The paid unlocked version is way to expensive considering the clunky user interface.
